title: Console A/B testing: create → validate → start experiment flow (UX + copy + edge cases)
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Goal
Design the end-to-end Console workflow to create an A/B experiment at a route level, validate config, and start/stop safely. This ticket covers UX + copy for the creation flow (results dashboard is DES-143).

Context
Route-level A/B testing is Console-first. Customers will split production traffic for a specific route (e.g., /v1/chat/completions) across model variants/configs, with deterministic assignment and standardized measurement hooks (latency, TTFT, cost, errors, exposures). Key risk areas: overlapping rollouts, confusing terminology (“control”), misconfiguration leading to regressions, and safety guardrails.

Artifacts / links
- Figma (Create + Validate + Start flow): https://figma.com/file/RI-AB-CreateFlow/DES-142-create-validate-start
- Prototype (clickthrough): https://figma.com/proto/RI-AB-CreateFlow/DES-142-proto
- Confluence design spec (draft): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CONSOLE/Route-level+A-B+testing+Console+workflows
- Copy doc (WIP): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RI-ab-copy-DES142
- Engineering epic (Console CRUD APIs): ENG-2843

Primary users
- ML/Platform engineers running production model changes
- Product teams validating new model variants/configs with minimal risk

Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Statistical methodology details (belongs in results dashboard spec + Applied ML)
- Bandit / automated optimization
- Arbitrary customer-defined metric ingestion

User story
As a project owner, I can create an experiment for a specific API route, choose two variants (model + key config deltas), allocate traffic, validate for conflicts/safety, and start the experiment with guardrails and an audit trail.

Proposed IA (where this lives)
Console → Project → Routes → (select route) → Experiments tab → “Create experiment”
Alternative entry point supported: Console → Rollouts → Experiments (filtered by project/route)

Flow overview
1) Create experiment (draft)
2) Validate & review (blocking checks + warnings)
3) Start experiment (confirmations + scheduling)
4) Running state (high-level status + quick links to results + stop/rollback)

1) Create experiment (Draft)
Fields
- Experiment name (required; unique per project)
- Route (pre-filled if launched from a route page)
- Description (optional)
- Variants (2 in v1)
  - Variant A: Model + config (temperature, max_tokens, top_p, system prompt template pointer if supported) + capacity tier (Hosted vs Dedicated)
  - Variant B: Model + config
- Traffic split (slider + numeric inputs)
  - Default: 90/10 (A/B)
  - Support 50/50 preset
- Assignment key (choice, with guidance)
  - Default: “API key” stickiness (api_key_id)
  - Optional: “End-user” stickiness via header (e.g., x-redwood-user-id) with explicit warning about cardinality/PII and stability requirements
- Eligibility filters (v1 minimal)
  - Region (optional; default all)
  - Environment (prod/staging) shown if project has both

UX notes
- Variants displayed as “Variant A (baseline)” and “Variant B (candidate)” by default. Avoid “control” unless the user explicitly labels it.
- Side-by-side diff panel: show only fields that differ between A and B (model name, quantization profile, max_tokens, etc.) to reduce cognitive load.

2) Validate & review step
Purpose
Make conflicts and safety issues explicit before any traffic shifts. Validation runs on demand and automatically on changes.

Validation outcomes
- Blocking errors (must fix)
- Warnings (allowed but must acknowledge at start)

Blocking checks (v1)
- Route is missing / not eligible (deleted route, wrong project)
- Traffic split invalid (must sum to 100; min 1% per variant; max 99% per variant)
- Variants identical (no meaningful diff)
- Variant model not available in selected region/tier
- Missing assignment input for selected stickiness (e.g., user-id header mode selected but header not configured)
- Overlapping rollout conflicts (see below)

Warnings (v1)
- Large shift recommended caution: any allocation >50% to a new variant triggers “consider starting at 10%” warning
- Config likely to change cost/latency materially (heuristic warnings; PM to confirm: e.g., max_tokens increased >2x)
- No stop schedule set (if they don’t set duration/end time)
- Multiple active experiments on same project (allowed if different routes, but warn if too many for interpretability)

Overlapping rollouts edge case (key requirement)
We need clear customer-facing behavior when an experiment is created on a route that already has:
- an active canary rollout, or
- a pinned model version with fallback policies.

Proposed UX behavior
- Console shows a “Routing precedence” callout in Validate & review:
  - “Experiments apply after route eligibility checks and before fallback routing. Fallback may override experiment assignment if a variant becomes unhealthy or unavailable.”
- If an active canary exists on the same route, we block start by default with an actionable error:
  - “This route has an active canary rollout (Rollout: <name>). Stop or complete the canary before starting an experiment.”
  - Rationale: reduces ambiguous interpretation of results and avoids compounded routing policies.
- If a pinned model exists without active canary, we allow experiments (since experiment variants can reference pinned model versions explicitly), but we warn if the experiment variant references an unpinned “latest” model alias.

Copy (draft)
- Error title: “Conflicting rollout detected”
- Error body: “Only one traffic-shaping policy can be active per route in Beta. Stop the rollout or choose a different route.”

3) Start experiment
Start options
- Start now
- Schedule start time (optional)
- Optional end time / duration (recommended; default 7 days suggestion)

Confirmations
- “Starting this experiment will shift X% of traffic on <route>.”
- If warnings exist, user must check acknowledgements:
  - “I understand this may increase latency/cost”
  - “I understand fallback can override assignment during incidents”

Post-start state
- Toast + persistent banner on route page: “Experiment running: <name> (A 90% / B 10%)” with quick actions: View results, Stop experiment.

Stop / rollback behavior (in-scope for copy + UX entry points)
- Stop experiment action available from:
  - Experiments list
  - Experiment details header
  - Route banner
- Stop modal offers:
  - “Stop and send 100% traffic to Variant A” (default)
  - “Stop and send 100% traffic to Variant B” (advanced; requires extra confirmation)
  - Copy: avoid “rollback” wording in customer UI; use “Stop experiment” and “Choose traffic destination”

Permission / RBAC notes (needs alignment with ENG-2847)
We should display the action but disable with tooltip if user lacks permission:
- “You don’t have permission to start/stop experiments. Ask a project admin.”

Accessibility requirements (checklist)
- All warnings/errors must be readable by screen readers; use proper alert roles in implementation.
- Traffic split slider must have keyboard input and numeric fields.
- Color is not the only indicator for Variant A/B; include labels and icons.

Open questions (needs PM + Eng input)
1) Terminology: “Experiment” vs “A/B test” in primary UI. Proposal: use “Experiment” in nav and headers; use “A/B test” in helper text.
2) Should we allow >2 variants in create flow (UI-wise) but gate server-side to 2? Proposal: do not expose add-variant UI in Beta to avoid backtracking.
3) Should we allow starting an experiment if a canary is running but the canary is on a different model family? Proposal: still block in Beta.
4) Default split: PM suggests 90/10; Eng suggests 95/5 to reduce risk. Proposal in mocks: 90/10 (editable) with a “Start small” preset.
5) Assignment key default: api_key_id is most reliable, but some customers want end-user stickiness. Proposal: default api_key_id; show user-id header as advanced with strong guidance.

Acceptance criteria
- Figma includes:
  - Create draft screen (empty + filled states)
  - Validate & review screen with examples of:
    - blocking error (overlapping rollout)
    - warning acknowledgements
  - Start modal (now/schedule + warning acknowledgements)
  - Running banner on route + primary actions
- Copy doc includes final strings for:
  - error/warning titles and bodies
  - tooltips for disabled actions (RBAC)
  - helper text for stickiness selection
- Edge cases explicitly addressed in UI:
  - overlapping rollouts (block)
  - missing stickiness header (block if selected)
  - identical variants (block)

Implementation notes for Engineering (FYI)
- UI should treat “Validate” as idempotent; allow retries.
- Validation payload should return structured codes so UI can group into Errors vs Warnings (ENG-2843).
- We should display the evaluation order/precedence in a stable callout to reduce support load.

Activity / comments
2026-02-03 (Kenji Nakamura): Added Validate & review step; included precedence callout and conflict blocking for active canaries. Need confirmation from platform on exact precedence language.
2026-02-05 (Marissa Cole): Prefer we avoid the word “control” in UI; customers interpret it as “safe.” Baseline/candidate is better.
2026-02-06 (Dylan Brooks): +1 to blocking overlapping canary in Beta. For pinned models, warning is fine. We should make sure error message points to the rollout by name with deep link.
2026-02-11 (Chloe Martin): Validation API can return both errors and warnings; please provide final list of codes you want surfaced as warnings vs hard blocks.
2026-02-14 (Paula Mendes): Reminder: metrics tags must not include freeform variant names; UI should show friendly names but backend uses variant_id. Please keep copy consistent: “Variant A/B” not “blue/green.”
2026-02-18 (Tessa Morgan): Reviewed latest mocks. Request: add a short “What happens during fallback?” inline disclosure to prevent surprise when guardrails override experiment routing.
